name: ssl-4k-e-drum-bus
description: Punchy, weighty 'British console' drum bus from the SSL 4K E (SL 4000 E channel strip) alone — the SSL counterpart to the tight-70s-api / blackbird-a5 (API = forward) and warm Studer/Neve (tape) directions. Uses the '242 Black' EQ (its 'legendary low-end weight' — measured: Black put the most energy in the low band of the three colours) for a kick-bell thump + de-box + light presence, and the channel VCA comp at 4:1 with FAST attack OUT (slow = transients pass) for punch from the dynamics, not the EQ. Measured on watercolors bus_punchy_pre (60 s dry drum bus): crest 21.6 -> 23.2 (punch UP), spectral centroid stays warm (2223 -> ~2272, NOT brighter), L/R corr 0.983, mono-sum loss 0.64 dB. The punch is the comp; the weight is the Black EQ.
intended_for: a dry-ish, measured-balanced drum bus/loop — SSL 4K E supplies low-end weight (Black EQ) + de-box + slow-attack VCA punch in one box (SSL = clean/weighty/controlled, the contrast to API forwardness and tape warmth)
plugin_build: SSL 4K E.vst3 (VST3 — renders headless via Pedalboard; iLok/PACE, authorized on this machine; RE-VERIFY on any other rig with presets/vst/probe_plugin.py 'SSL 4K E')
headless_notes: ALMOST EVERY SSL 4K E param is a discrete/enum (Pedalboard valid_values). FLOAT-valued ones (lf_gain_db, *_frequency_*, *_q, compressor_threshold_db/release_s, mic_db, width, input/output_trim_db) can go through apply-vst-chain's float dict. STRING enums — compressor_ratio ('4.0','∞'), fader_level_db, pan, eq_colour (Brown/Black/Orange), lf_type/hf_type (Shelf/Bell), and every Out/In routing toggle — CANNOT: apply-vst-chain reports them 'set' but the value silently does not take (measured: compressor_ratio=4 via the float dict gave crest 22.3 vs this harness's exact '4.0' string => 23.2). This harness's setattr handles them; it also snaps log-stepped string enums like high_pass_filter_hz to the nearest valid value. output is peak-trimmed by the harness so the comp makeup-gain level jump is handled.
notes: EQ COLOUR is the SSL 4K E's signature lever and the three are genuinely different at IDENTICAL dial settings (measured, same +4 LF / +3 HMF / +4 HF on the dry bus): '02 Brown' = brightest top + air (centroid +202, the original 'gritty/musical' E EQ); '242 Black' = fattest LOW band + smoother top ('legendary low-end weight' — why this drum-bus preset uses it for kick weight); '132 Orange' = the rare PASSIVE EQ, gentlest top but nearly DOUBLES the 2.5-5 kHz presence (hi-mid ratio 0.034->0.068) => most forward mids, 'great for kick & snare'. Pick the colour for the tone you want, THEN dial.

The COMP'S FAST BUTTON is the punch lever, and it is TEXTBOOK here (the OPPOSITE of the UAD API Vision strip): FAST attack OUT (slower/auto attack) lets transients through -> crest UP (4:1 slow 23.1, 10:1 slow 25.1 vs dry 21.6); FAST attack IN (~1 ms, the classic 'grabby' SSL VCA) catches transients -> crest DOWN (21.3) + brighter/denser. For measured punch keep FAST OUT; engage FAST for aggressive transient control / density (lower crest).

Punch is the COMP, weight is the EQ. The Black LF bell @ 80 + de-box @ 450 gave weight without raising centroid; the slow comp gave the crest. Do NOT chase punch with top-end boosts (the E EQ is constant-Q — it will not auto-narrow like API/SSL-G proportional-Q, so a big top boost just gets bright).

compressor_auto_make_up=true raises the body up to peaks => part of why crest rises; it also pushes true-peak, so the harness peak-trims to -1 dBFS. Re-set compressor_threshold_db to YOUR source level (this was tuned to a ~-23 LUFS dry bus); a hotter bus needs a higher threshold for the same GR.

For a brighter/airier or grittier variant, switch eq_colour to 'Brown' and/or drive the preamp with mic_db (the MIC knob, 0-50 — adds console grit, 'spice on kick/snare/bass'); for max forward mid snap on a kick/snare bus, try 'Orange'. Re-measure centroid/crest after any colour change.
